newsitem.title: UK: EMERGING MARKET DEBT STEADY,QUIET AHEAD OF US DATA.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING MARKET DEBT STEADY,QUIET AHEAD OF US DATA.

text.p: Emerging market debt held steady on Wednesday but trade was reduced to a trickle as investors awaited direction from U.S. Treasuries and the release of July U.S. retail sales at 1230 GMT.
"Everyone is waiting for retail sales. The market is focused on those figures like a rabbit in a headlight," said one trader.

Dealers reported modest demand for Russian paper at around previous levels as Russia continued its recent strong run. But business elsewhere was very thin, although the underlying tone remained positive.
"The Brady market is really quite well-bid considering the weakness we've seen in Treasuries. Spreads remain tight," commented one dealer.
Dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank loans were unchanged at 102-1/8 bid as were the PRINS at 74 and IANs at 81-1/8.
Bulgaria FRBs were up 1/8 at 62-1/2 and Poland Pars added 1/2 to 58-5/8.
Latin American debt was quiet with Argentine FRBs and Brazil's "C" bonds both off 1-8 at 95-1/2 and 82-5/8 respectively.

Wednesday's U.S. July retail sales are expected to be strong after a second quarter lull. A Reuter poll of economists forecast a rise of 0.7 percent in the headline retail sales and 0.5 percent ex-autos.
Also due at 1230 GMT are July producer prices, which are expected to show a mild 0.1 percent rise after a 0.1 percent drop the previous month.
